claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking you about your child(ren).

**How old is the child you're claiming Child Benefit for?** 

Please let me know:
- Are they **under 16 years old**, **between 16 and 19 years old**, or **20 or older**?

If you're claiming for multiple children, just let me know about each one and their age category. This will help me determine which eligibility path to follow.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 21 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing that information! Since Alex is 21 years old (20 or over), let me navigate to the relevant outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry, but based on the information you've provided, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

**Here's why:**

Child Benefit can only be claimed for:
- Children under 16 years old, OR
- Children aged 16-19 who are in approved education or training

Since Alex is 21 years old and no longer falls into either of these categories, he does not qualify as a "qualifying child" for Child Benefit purposes.

**Important to note:** If Alex was previously receiving Child Benefit and recently turned 20, the benefit would have stopped at that point (or up to 20 weeks after leaving education if he left between ages 16-19 and was registered with a careers service or armed forces).

If you have any other children you'd like me to check eligibility for, I'd be happy to help with those!

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Oh, I see. That's disappointing, but I understand. He's too old now. Thanks for explaining that to me.

Just to be clear though - he doesn't live with me anymore, but I do help him out with about £20 a week for bits and pieces. Does that make any difference at all, or is it still just down to his age?

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good question! No, unfortunately the financial support you're providing doesn't change the outcome. **It's purely down to his age.**

Child Benefit eligibility is determined by specific age criteria and education/training status - not by whether the child lives with you or by any financial support you provide to them. Since Alex is 21 years old, he falls outside the age limits for Child Benefit regardless of the circumstances.

The £20 a week you're helping him with is generous support, but it doesn't affect Child Benefit eligibility in any way.

**Is there anything else I can help you with?** For example:
- Do you have any other children you'd like me to check eligibility for?
- Do you have any other questions about Child Benefit?

I'm here to help!

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex is my only child. Thank you for checking and explaining everything clearly - I appreciate your help. At least I know where I stand now.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help clarify the situation for you. It's good to know where you stand, even if it's not the outcome you were hoping for.

If you ever have any questions about Child Benefit in the future, or if your circumstances change (for example, if you were to have or care for any other children), feel free to come back and I'd be happy to help you check eligibility again.

Thank you for using this service, and all the best to you and Alex!

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Thank you so much, that's very kind. Take care!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: You're welcome! Take care, and best wishes to you! 👋
